calls.title: Demo Call - GrowthBook<>GlossGenius
calls.summary:
# MEDDICC Sales Call Summary

Call on [date of demo] with Lanny McNie (TPM, formerly GlassGenius/now Genius AI), Kesavan Kushalnagar (Engineer, Application Platform Team), Chandini Ramesh (Data Analyst, Product Analytics), Jake Heier (Account Executive, GrowthBook), and Logan Bates (Solutions Engineer, GrowthBook, former Statsig employee).

## Attendees & Titles
Lanny McNie served as primary point of contact and technical coordinator with five years tenure at the organization (employee #15). Kesavan Kushalnagar, an engineer on the application platform team, owned the technical replacement work for their legacy feature flagging system. Chandini Ramesh from the data team brought experimentation infrastructure expertise. Jake Heier and Logan Bates represented GrowthBook as account and solutions engineer respectively.

## Quantifiable Outcomes & Metrics
GlossGenius (rebranded as Genius AI) currently managed 1,000+ active feature flags with 15-25 concurrent experiments running. The organization operated a 10-year-old platform requiring immediate migration due to their existing EPO solution being sunset by Datadog's acquisition.

## Budget Authority & Decision Signals
Lanny explicitly stated cost structure evaluation as a personal priority, requesting detailed pricing models aligned with their specific usage patterns. The organization had already received migration pricing from Datadog (current platform owner) and was actively evaluating alternatives, indicating serious budget authority and decision-making capability within this group.

## Technical Requirements
Kesavan identified several critical technical specifications: REST API and SDK stability with advance notice before breaking changes (citing previous EPO issues with hashing algorithm modifications), self-hosting versus cloud deployment options, and seamless integration with their existing feature service architecture that pulls configurations and performs flag evaluation via SDKs without direct embedding.

## Decision Process & Timeline
The sales cycle appeared accelerated due to EPO's sunset timeline. The organization had pre-shortlisted GrowthBook alongside Datadog and likely other alternatives. Three key stakeholders attended—engineering, product analytics, and technical program management—suggesting a collaborative evaluation process.

## Specific Pain Points
The primary pain point was forced migration due to platform acquisition and sunset. Secondary frustration centered on Datadog's incompatibility despite owning the legacy platform, as they rebuilt rather than ported EPO. The organization specifically wanted to avoid fragmenting functionality across multiple tools, preferring unified feature flagging and experimentation.

## Champion Signals
Lanny demonstrated strong champion characteristics: five-year tenure providing organizational knowledge, self-identified as "as much a point of contact as you're going to have," explicitly stated GrowthBook appeared "really compatible," invited cross-functional stakeholders, and positioned himself as intermediary between engineering and leadership.

## Competitors Mentioned
Datadog (owns EPO), Optimizely (legacy platform), and LaunchDarkly (short-term solution) were discussed. Datadog represented the primary competitive threat with migration assistance and existing relationship advantages.

## Next Steps
Jake Heier requested detailed technical requirements documentation from Kesavan to align GrowthBook's capabilities against their specifications. The conversation continued regarding self-hosting options and API stability guarantees. Timeline remained approximately 30 minutes for initial discovery, suggesting follow-up technical deep dives were anticipated.
